chapter: Chano Pozo, Town Hall and Charlie Parker
title: Flip Phillips versus Charlie Parker as soloists
summary: Machito says Flip Phillips was more flexible, while Parker was an intellectual in chords and creativity.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Macho, I heard all your recordings, I first bought them on 78s. Now I have them on long-play, like "Bucabu", "Flying Home", "Tanga", why did you use Flip Phillips more than Charlie Parker or any other saxophonist? Was there a reason?
Ahh - Flip Phillips was more flexible than Charlie Parker.
Ehh - maybe he was Italian and the Italian has something in common with Spanish and he was, in a way, easy to record all of different type of numbers than with Charlie Parker.
I agree with you. Listening to those recordings, Flip was more melodic and more in tune with the Cuban music than Charlie Parker was.

And this is another thing, ahh - with all the respect of Flip Phillips, he didn't have the imagination of Charlie Parker, so every person has its limitations and his limitations sometimes make more understandable; because if a fellow with limitations listens to a fellow with limitations they get together very well. You are talking with an intellectual and you are third-grade or fourth-grade in grammar, how could you understand an intellectual? So to me Charlie Parker was an intelectual in his analysis in chords and in creativity.
